subject.title: Feature: Granular Discord action gates (split actions.messages into read/edit/delete)

question: Should OpenClaw add Discord channel/account-level granular message gates for send/read/edit/delete, or should the existing generic tool/action policy remain the supported way to remove destructive message actions?
rationale: Both directions are technically viable, but the choice changes public config shape, per-account inheritance, generated metadata, and least-privilege semantics for destructive Discord message actions.

options.title: Add Discord Granular Gates
options.body: Implement a backward-compatible Discord `actions.messages` sub-gate or equivalent top-level gates that distinguish send, read, edit, and delete while preserving the current boolean shorthand.

options.title: Document Generic Policy Only
options.body: Keep `channels.discord.actions.messages` coarse and document the supported generic allow/deny policy for deployments that need to remove destructive message actions.

options.title: Defer For Cross-Channel Design
options.body: Keep this issue open until maintainers choose a broader cross-channel action-gate model instead of adding a Discord-specific shape now.

recommendation.title: Add Discord Granular Gates
recommendation.body: Implement a backward-compatible Discord `actions.messages` sub-gate or equivalent top-level gates that distinguish send, read, edit, and delete while preserving the current boolean shorthand.

likelyOwner.reason: The runtime split plus prior review context make steipete the best available owner for the Discord config/security contract decision.
